# Configuring and Running a TIRREX Demo

## A demo is just configuration {.tirrex-overview-slide}

::: {.tirrex-story-intro}
TIRREX Roboterrium is built on top of the ROMEA ecosystem to simplify the use of both ROMEA and ROS 2. Rather than implementing its own launch logic, a demo only describes the robot, devices, capabilities, and execution mode through YAML configuration files. TIRREX orchestrates this configuration and relies on ROMEA to launch the required ROS 2 components. This approach enables the same demo to run seamlessly in simulation, on a real robot, or within record-and-replay workflows, without modification.
:::

![](img/02_configuring_tirrex_demo/demo_is_configuration.svg){.demo-is-configuration-diagram}

::: {.highlight-box .tirrex-provides-points}
::: {.tirrex-provides-grid}
::: {.tirrex-provides-item}
**TIRREX provides**

Experiment-level orchestration<br>

Same workflow for simulation and field tests
:::

::: {.tirrex-provides-item}

Component launch logic<br>

:::

::: {.tirrex-provides-item}

## A configuration example {.tirrex-story-slide}

::: {.tirrex-story-intro}
All information specific to a demo is grouped in one readable,
version-controlled directory. It is the single source of truth shared by
simulation, field execution and replay.
:::

::: {.columns .configuration-directory-layout}
::: {.column width="65%"}
### What the directory contains

::: {.configuration-directory-points}
- `robot/` — robot system and algorithm configuration
- `simulation.yaml` — simulator, world and initial poses
- `wgs84_anchor.yaml` — geographic reference shared by the demo
- `records.yaml` — recording options
- `paths/` — trajectories used by navigation
:::

### Inside the `robot/` directory

::: {.configuration-directory-conventions}
- `base.yaml` describes the mobile base
- `devices.yaml` lists the available devices
- `devices/<name>.<type>.yaml` describes each embedded devices
- `localisation.yaml`, `path_matching.yaml` and `path_following.yaml` configure localisation and navigation
- `teleop.yaml` configures manual robot control
:::
:::

::: {.column .configuration-directory-tree width="35%"}
::: {.config-path}
```text
config/
  robot/
    base.yaml
    devices.yaml
    devices/
      *.gps.yaml
      *.imu.yaml
      *.lidar.yaml
      *.camera.yaml
      *.implement.yaml
    localisation.yaml
    path_matching.yaml
    path_following.yaml
    teleop.yaml
  simulation.yaml
  wgs84_anchor.yaml
  records.yaml
  paths/
    *.traj
```
:::

::: {.multi-robot-note}
The same layout can be extended to several robot directories, each with its
own ROS 2 namespace.
:::
:::
:::

## How to launch a demo {.generic-launch-slide}

::: {.tirrex-story-intro}
Once the directory is defined, every demo uses the same TIRREX entry point.
Only the configuration, namespace and execution mode change.
:::

::: {.command-spacer}
:::

```bash
ros2 launch tirrex_core core.launch.py \
  demo_configuration_directory:=/path/to/tirrex_adap2e/config \
  robot_namespace:=adap2e mode:=simulation_gazebo

ros2 launch tirrex_core robot/robot_localisation.launch.py \
  robot_configuration_directory:=/path/to/tirrex_adap2e/config/robot \
  robot_namespace:=adap2e mode:=simulation_gazebo

ros2 launch tirrex_core robot/robot_path_following.launch.py \
  demo_configuration_directory:=/path/to/tirrex_adap2e/config \
  robot_namespace:=adap2e mode:=simulation_gazebo
```

::: {.command-spacer}
:::

::: {.columns .launch-parameter-overview}
::: {.column width="52%"}
### Launch parameters

::: {.launch-parameters}
- `demo_configuration_directory` — specifies the path to the demo configuration directory
- `robot_namespace` — sets the robot ROS 2 namespace
- `mode` — selects the execution environment
:::
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
### Available modes

::: {.launch-modes}
- `live` — starts the robot, devices and algorithms
- `simulation_<simulator>` — starts the simulator, spawns the robot and runs the algorithms<br><span class="simulator-values">Available values: `gazebo` · `isaac` · `4dv`</span>
:::
:::
:::

::: {.reference-demo-note}
The reference configuration is available in
[Tirrex-Roboterrium/tirrex_adap2e](https://github.com/Tirrex-Roboterrium/tirrex_adap2e)
and is used throughout the rest of this presentation.
:::

## What is launched

The Adap2e simulation launches a complete robot runtime: mobile-base and
virtual-implement controllers, Gazebo sensor bridges, localisation, and path
following.

- Path following and teleoperation both publish to `base/cmd_mux`, where
  higher-priority manual commands take precedence.
- Additional command sources can register with the same multiplexer without
  changing the mobile-base controller.
- The virtual implement follows the same command pipeline: teleoperation,
  command mux, then controller.

![](img/02_configuring_tirrex_demo/what_is_launched.svg){.what-is-launched-diagram}
